                                  13
                                                         Defendant.
                                  14

                                  15           The issue before the court, whether John Does 1-3, et al. v. Roblox Corporation, Case No.

                                  16   26-cv-00271 (the “Class Action”) ought to be a member case in or related to In re: Roblox

                                  17   Corporation Child Sexual Exploitation and Assault Litigation, MDL. No. 3166 (“In re: Roblox”)

                                  18   may have arisen from simple confusion as to whether Plaintiffs sought to file as a direct member

                                  19   case1 in In re: Roblox or instead to be related for purposes of Local Rule 3-12 without being a

                                  20   member case to In re: Roblox.2 Nonetheless, having reviewed the parties’ briefing, the Court finds

                                  21   that the Class Action is properly related to In re: Roblox for purposes of Local Rule 3-12 but

                                  22   should not be included as a member case in In re: Roblox. Per the multidistrict litigation (“MDL”)

                                  23
                                       1
                                  24     It is not clear from Platiniff’s motion, Dkt. 10, whether they seek relation in the sense of Local
                                       Rule 3-12 only or seek membership in the MDL, as Defendant Roblox seems to mean “relation” it
                                  25   its motion, Dkt. 8. The cover sheet to Plaintiff’s initial filing does not characterize the origin of the
                                       Class Action suit as a “Multidistrict Litigation-Direct Filing” but instead indicates the suit is an
                                  26   “Original Proceeding” related to In re: Roblox. Dkt. 1.
                                       2
                                  27    A case may be related to an MDL for purposes of Local Rule 3-12 without being a member case.
                                       See e.g., Order Relating Case and Order of Recusal, Microsoft Corp. v. Compression Labs, Inc.,
                                  28   No. 05-cv-1567-JF, Dkt. 14, (N.D. Cal. May 6, 2005).
                                          Case 3:26-cv-00271-RS          Document 11          Filed 02/17/26    Page 2 of 2




                                   1   panel transfer order, In re: Roblox pertains to the sexual exploitation and, in some cases, assault of

                                   2   minors by child predators who targeted and groomed minors through the Roblox gaming platform.

                                   3   MDL No. 3166, Dkt. 1 (“Transfer Order”) at 1. The Class Action, by contrast, alleges Plaintiffs’

                                   4   injuries relate to “illicit” and “inappropriate” “conversations,” “contact,” and “behavior” without

                                   5   alleging exploitation or assault. Accordingly, the Class Action is not properly part of the In re:

                                   6   Roblox.

                                   7          On the other hand, Civil Local Rule 3-12 defines related cases, such that they will be heard

                                   8   before the same Judge, as actions “concern[ing] substantially the same parties, property,

                                   9   transaction, or event” where “[i]t appears likely that there will be an unduly duplication of labor or

                                  10   expense or conflicting results if the cases are conducted before different Judges.” Although the

                                  11   Class Action and In re: Roblox differ with regard to the harm alleged to the plaintiffs in each, they

                                  12   share the key defendant party, Roblox, and allegations related to that defendant’s conduct enabling
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   the grooming of minor children on its platform. This is sufficient for relation under Local Rule 3-

                                  14   12. Accordingly, the Class Action is not a member case in In re: Roblox but related for purposes

                                  15   of Local Rule 3-12.

                                  16

                                  17   IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                  18
                                  19   Dated: February 17, 2026

                                                                                        RICHARD SEEBORG

                                  15          On February 4, 2026, Defendant Roblox Corporation filed an Administrative Motion

                                  16   Opposing Relation of this putative class action to In re: Roblox Corporation Child Sexual

                                  17   Exploitation and Assault Litigation, MDL No. 3166 (“MDL”). Plaintiff is ordered to file

                                  18   responsive briefing as to its position regarding relation to the MDL by February 25, 2026.

                                  19          Counsel for Plaintiffs is also ordered to show cause by February 25, 2026 as to why Civil

                                  20   Local Rule 11-3(c)(2), which disqualifies a pro hac vice applicant who is regularly engaged in the

                                  21   practice of law in the State of California, does not apply in this instance to Paul J. Doolittle’s

                                  22   Motion for Leave to Appear in Pro Hac Vice, MDL Dkt. 159.

                                  23
